analysis_steps.goal: Estimate LSB continuum level from USB

method.value: Decompose USB continuum into dust 50%, free-free 25%, synchrotron 25% and scale with spectral indices 3.5, -0.15, -1.0

evidence.quote: we estimate the LSB continuum level to be 11.26 mJy beam$^{-1}$.

assumptions.value: Component fractions and spectral indices as above

evidence.quote: thermal dust emission from both the dusty torus and the extended cold dust (50 per cent contribution to the total USB emission)

validation.value: Varying free-free to synchrotron ratio changes estimate only slightly

evidence.quote: Note that varying the free$-$free to synchrotron ratio only slightly modify this estimation

analysis_steps.goal: Search LSB spectrum for H26alpha and set upper limit

method.value: Extract spectrum at AGN position with single aperture; compare excess to 3 sigma

evidence.quote: this excess in each channel is still below the 3$\sigma$ limit of our observations (1.26 mJy beam$^{-1}$)

assumptions.value: Integrated limit assumes Gaussian profile with FWHM 3000 km/s

evidence.quote: The integrated intensity was calculated by assuming the Gaussian profile with the FWHM of 3000 km s$^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: Model BLR cloud line and continuum optical depth and expected flux

method.value: LTE line and free-free optical depths for Ne=1e9, Te=1e4 K, L=20 Rsun; line-to-continuum ratio; scale to NGC 1068 with covering factor and r_in

evidence.quote: we obtain an optical depth of H26$\alpha$ as $\tau_{\rm H26\alpha}$ $\sim$ 3.4

assumptions.value: LTE, uniform density and temperature clouds, stimulated emission by non-thermal background neglected

evidence.quote: A potential contamination due to stimulated emission caused by the background non-thermal radiation is neglected for simplicity.

findings_qualitative.value: BLR clouds with Ne~1e9 cm^-3 dominate broad submm-RL flux; other densities are too optically thick or thin

evidence.quote: BLR clouds with $N_e$ $\sim$ 10$^9$ cm$^{-3}$ would be the dominant contributor to the H$n\alpha$ flux.

claims.hypothesis: Is broad or narrow H26alpha detectable toward NGC 1068 with ALMA?
claims.experiment: Cycle 2 Band 7 spectrum at AGN position with estimated continuum
claims.finding: Non-detection, not conclusive given continuum uncertainty

evidence.quote: here we report on the non-detection of both broad and narrow H26$\alpha$ emission line

claims.hypothesis: Which BLR clouds can emit submm-RLs and can they be detected?
claims.experiment: LTE optical depth and line-to-continuum calculations
claims.result: Expected flux ~0.011 Jy/km/s, peak a few to 10 microJy

evidence.quote: it is virtually impossible to achieve a high sensitivity enough to detect the above flux significantly (e.g., 10$\sigma$ detection) even with ALMA

why_this_method.value: Submm-RLs avoid dust extinction and maser amplification, enabling BLR probes of obscured AGN

evidence.quote: we considered that submillimetre H i RLs (submm-RLs, hereafter) would provide a way as they do not suffer from dust extinction.

limitations_admitted.value: LSB covers only part of the broad line, so continuum level is highly uncertain

evidence.quote: Continuum subtraction can be problematic in the LSB because all channels would contain the BLR component due to the limited band width.

referee_caveats_inferred: Continuum level assumption (50/25/25 split) drives the marginal excess
Single uniform-cloud model with no uncertainties
